title: introduce-go-wasm-proxy-quickstart--lightweight-rag-edge-and-local-dev
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Adds a minimal Go-based RAG quickstart that shows a small WASM tool-proxy pattern for edge and local dev. Motivation: teams asked for a compact Go example that demonstrates a browser/edge-hosted WASM tool adapter + a tiny Go proxy that performs model calls to Redwood, manages a cached embeddings layer, and exposes a single streaming endpoint for client-side agents. This quickstart is intended for engineers who want a small production-lean pattern (Go server, WASM tool adapters, DevContainer) rather than large Node/TS stacks. Changes include: - quickstart code (server, wasm tool adapter, example tool wasm build) - docs/step-by-step guide with troubleshooting and cost/perf tips - devcontainer to replicate local edge flow - GitHub Actions workflow to run unit tests and wasm build. Checklist: - [x] minimal working server and wasm tool example - [x] docs walkthrough and callouts about batching, KV caching, and streaming SLOs - [x] CI to build wasm and run go tests - [x] add badges and quick links in quickstarts index Notable constraints and tradeoffs described in docs: small wasm tools are suitable for stateless helpers (parsers, small scrapers, sanitizers). For heavy compute use server-side tools or Redwood Dedicated. Related Linear items: ENG-9821 (quickstart request), PM-3410 (docs placement).
